attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his exact wording, including 'over a billion dollars' and 'universally-loathed'. It is a compound retrospective observation wrapped in sarcasm, but its parts can be checked.

contract.note: Reading 'universally-loathed' as widespread, overwhelmingly negative reception already allows for exaggeration and is ordinary. The monetary parts have no stated threshold or basis, so they depend on interpretation.

evidence.note: Independent ACSI survey of US users, March 2026, published before the post. Copilot scored 74, second of six and above ChatGPT. That is not overwhelmingly negative reception, though it covers US users only.

Microsoft's own disclosure of $37B AI annualized run rate for its whole AI business. Annualized, broader scope, and a company statement, so it does not settle realized revenue or the 'break out' wording.
CMA decision with the consideration figure redacted. It cannot settle the billion-dollar threshold either way.

reviews.rationale: This is a compound claim. One stated part, the 'universally-loathed chatbot', is materially contradicted by independent ACSI data showing above-average Copilot satisfaction. The rest is unresolved: the deal value is redacted, there is no benchmark evidence on 'mid-tier', capex has no threshold, and the revenue disclosure is annualized. Because one part of the conjunction fails under a fair reading, the claim as stated is contradicted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Verbatim causal claim: the three companies' GPU buying was driven by Microsoft's GPU buying.

contract.note: Requiring material, not sole, causation fits his 'because'. Placing the episode after ChatGPT matches the surrounding text.

evidence.note: Meta's own earnings remarks give an alternative rationale, Llama compute needs. They neither confirm nor rule out Microsoft's influence.
Amazon shareholder letter dated April 2025 ties spending to AWS demand. Self-description; it does not address Microsoft.
Secondary reproduction of Pichai's call remarks on the risk of underinvesting. Fits general competitive pressure but gives no Microsoft-specific link.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is company self-explanations, which offer alternative motives without excluding Microsoft's influence. No decision records or procurement chronology link Microsoft's purchases to procurement at Amazon, Google or Meta, and none establish independent decisions either. The packet does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful to his wording. The drafter rightly left out the clause about defenders citing past bubbles, which is rhetoric. 'Infinite' is hyperbole, but the claim of dependence on outside funding can be checked.

contract.note: Reading 'infinite resources' as continuing dependence on outside financing is an ordinary reading. The contract chose the January–March 2026 period itself, and the speaker gave no cash-flow measure, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: Ars Technica report on OpenAI's audited 2025 accounts: large operating loss against $13B revenue. This is a different period and an accrual measure, not Q1 2026 cash flow.
GIC's February 2026 announcement confirms outside equity funding for Anthropic. It does not show that customer receipts cover nothing, or that Anthropic cannot sustain itself without it.

reviews.rationale: The evidence suggests both companies rely heavily on outside capital, but none of it covers cash flow or financing dependence for the contracted period, January–March 2026. Losses and fundraising alone do not meet the support or contradiction conditions. Unresolved on this packet.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts the statistic in his own voice in his own post.

semantics.note: The 61% figure is the checkable part of the sentence; the rest of it is rhetoric. The proposition keeps the figure, the metric and the year.

contract.note: The global value-share reading matches the source he linked and the plain wording. Rounding to the nearest point is fair.

evidence.note: OECD analysis of Preqin data, February 2026: $258.7B to AI out of $427.1B global VC in 2025, about 60.6%, stated as about 61%. Same scope and year.

reviews.rationale: Official OECD statistics put AI at about 61% of global 2025 VC investment by value, which matches the contract's scope and year. No comparable data in the packet give a different share.
